A STUDY IN LIGHT, SHADOW & GEOMETRY

Explore how light moves through Kryptos.

Kryptos is Jim Sanborn’s encrypted sculpture at CIA headquarters in Langley, Virginia. This interactive laboratory explores a hypothesis: could sunlight passing through its cut-out letters create patterns relevant to its fourth encrypted section, K4?

Examine how the date, time, light direction and assumed sculpture geometry change the projected light. About the sculpture · CIA · Evidence & assumptions

This is a research simulator, not a demonstrated solution. The reconstruction is not surveyed, and an apparent alignment is not evidence of the artist’s intent.

04 / RAW K4 · 97 CHARACTERS
Canonical K4 uses 31 columns, beginning at row 25, column 28. Full-screen mode preserves the complete cipher and tableau transcript lines (29–33 characters), at an assumed constant physical pitch. Its glyph shapes and spacing are unmeasured. Click a K4 letter to inspect its index.
Confirmed clues only · shown directly beneath each encrypted line. Mint letters are confirmed; neutral dots (·) are unknown. Positions count the first O as 1. This is not a solved message.
JSON restores optical inputs. Educational selection is included as reference metadata; it does not change the physical solver.
05 / EVIDENCE & PROVENANCE
Computationally verified
Geometric ray–plane intersections; shared aperture/material geometry for panel and shadow; 45° / 30° / 60° controls; 97-character transcript and indices; JSON roundtrip; historical DST; solar benchmarks within 0.3°.
Assumed & approximate
Full-screen mode includes both curved text regions, the surrounding cipher, a reverse-reading tableau, an assumed mid-height seam and an approximate tree at the cipher outer end. Two sine lobes, total chord span, heading, clearance and tree size remain hypotheses. CIA describes an 8 ft screen; an NSA summary says about 10 ft. These are competing documentary scenarios, not surveyed certainty. The isolated K4 control omits surrounding text and substitutes 27 blank copper cells for K3. Full-screen glyphs use equal physical stroke cells and approximate counter bridges; they are original generic shapes, not traced serifed hand-cut lettering. Physical pitch is assumed. Copper can be an ideal sheet or a normal-offset solid with aperture walls using separately reported ¼-inch and ½-inch scenarios. Finite uniform solar-disk sampling and tilted/bounded receiver patches are optional numerical experiments. Their preview convergence is not measured site accuracy. Refraction, limb darkening, self-shadow intensity on copper, pools, granite, fasteners, terrain, buildings and photo calibration are omitted. K2 coordinates are a reference location, not a survey.
How to read this experiment
Copper blocks sunlight: the dark ground silhouette is the union of its material shadows. The missing copper makes bright letters inside it. Light direction controls ground displacement; incidence depends on each curved surface normal. Camera angle only changes your view. Back views naturally mirror the openings. A projected center marker does not guarantee an unoccluded bright letter.
The ciphertext is intended to be read from the front; the alphabet tableau is intentionally oriented to be read from the back (CIA description). Both are through-cut apertures, not printed decals. Moving behind the screen mirrors glyph shapes and the spatial order within a row. That is distinct from reversing the canonical 97-letter K4 sequence or changing a geographic bearing by 180°. The entrance compass is a separate installation.
Unsupported observations & source record
Reported OBKR / NGKSSO / NFBNYP / AUEKCAR groupings are unverified user observations. The preset selects those letters only; it does not tune geometry or assert a match. This simulator preserves ciphertext and makes no decoding claim.
